author: historian-agent:gemini-flash-outline
title: Plato
summary: Plato, a philosopher of ancient Greece who wrote in the middle of the fourth century BCE, was the student of Socrates and the teacher of Aristotle, and founded the Academy. His most famous work, the Republic, is generally regarded as giving his own philosophy. The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy calls him one of the most penetrating, wide-ranging and influential authors in Western literature.

uncertainty.note: IEP notes widely accepted birth in 428-7 BCE and death at 348-7 BCE; SEP gives 429?–347 BCE; WHE notes the traditional birth year 428/427 BCE.

as_recorded.value: born in 428-7 B.C.E and died at the age of eighty or eighty-one at 348-7 B.C.E.

where.modern_name: Athens, Greece (birthplace, seat of the Academy, and place of death)

importance.justification: Foundational thinker whose dialogues and Athenian Academy established Western philosophical tradition, metaphysics, political theory, and educational institutions.

related.because: Plato was the student of Socrates, whose life, dialectical method, and execution motivated Plato's philosophical dialogues.
Aristotle studied at Plato's Academy for two decades before developing his own philosophical system.
The condemnation and death of Socrates profoundly altered Plato's view of Athenian democracy and spurred his political writings.

reviewer_note: Birth year differs: 429 with a question mark in one source, 428 or 427 in the other. The pin marks Athens.
